references.text: The Lord looked with favor on Abel's offering, which recalls God's acceptance of the sacrifice when flames rose from the altar.
Fire went out from the Lord and consumed the burnt offering on the altar, and the people fell face down, just as Manoah and his wife did.
Elijah was taken up to heaven, which recalls the angel's ascent in the flame from the altar.
The angel of the Lord touched the sacrifice with his staff, fire burst forth from the rock, and the angel vanished from Gideon's sight, a clear parallel to the event with Manoah.
Isaiah fell down in awe when he saw the glory of the Lord, just as Manoah and his wife fell on their faces.
Isaiah's vision of the Lord in the temple shows a similar awe and worship that Manoah and his wife experienced.
John fell down as if dead when he saw the glorified Christ, a reaction that reflects the awe of Manoah and his wife.
